trajectory_messages.content:
I'm using a CSS formatter and I've noticed that comments written inline within CSS property declarations are being moved to the wrong place.

*   When a CSS comment appears between a property name and the colon character in a CSS declaration (e.g., `color/* comment */:value`), the formatter must preserve the comment between the property name and the colon in the formatted output (e.g., `color /* comment */: value`), not move it before the property name.

*   When a CSS comment appears between the colon and the value in a CSS declaration (e.g., `color: /* comment */ blue`), the formatter must keep the comment immediately after the colon in the formatted output. The value must then be placed on the next line with one additional level of indentation (e.g., `color: /* comment */\n  blue`).

*   Multiple CSS comments between a property name and the colon must each be preserved in that position; similarly, multiple comments between the colon and the value must be preserved after the colon, with the value still placed on the next line.

*   Comments that already appear on their own line before a CSS property declaration (leading comments) must continue to be formatted correctly and must remain before the property name, not be affected by changes to colon/value comment handling.

*   The same comment-preservation rules for property name/colon/value positions must also apply to CSS declarations appearing inside at-rule conditions (such as feature-query conditions).

*   When no comment appears between the colon and the value, the value must remain on the same line as the property name and colon, with no extra line break introduced.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

266	    /// The closest parent node that fully encloses the comment.
267	    ///
268	    /// A node encloses a comment when the comment is between two of its direct children (ignoring lists).
269	    ///
270	    /// # Examples
271	    ///
272	    /// ```ignore
273	    /// [a, /* comment */ b]
274	    /// ```
275	    ///
276	    /// The enclosing node is the array expression and not the identifier `b` because
277	    /// `a` and `b` are children of the array expression and `comment` is a comment between the two nodes.
278	    pub fn enclosing_node(&self) -> &SyntaxNode<L> {
279	        &self.enclosing
280	    }
281	
282	    /// Returns the comment piece.
283	    pub fn piece(&self) -> &SyntaxTriviaPieceComments<L> {
284	        &self.comment
285	    }
286	
287	    /// Returns the node preceding the comment.
288	    ///
289	    /// The direct child node (ignoring lists) of the [`enclosing_node`](DecoratedComment::enclosing_node) that precedes this comment.
290	    ///
291	    /// Returns [None] if the [`enclosing_node`](DecoratedComment::enclosing_node) only consists of tokens or if
292	    /// all preceding children of the [`enclosing_node`](DecoratedComment::enclosing_node) have been tokens.
293	    ///
294	    /// The Preceding node is guaranteed to be a sibling of [`following_node`](DecoratedComment::following_node).
295	    ///
296	    /// # Examples
297	    ///
298	    /// ## Preceding tokens only
299	    ///
300	    /// ```ignore
301	    /// [/* comment */]
302	    /// ```
303	    /// Returns [None] because the comment has no preceding node, only a preceding `[` token.
304	    ///
305	    /// ## Preceding node
306	    ///
307	    /// ```ignore
308	    /// [a /* comment */, b]
309	    /// ```
310	    ///
311	    /// Returns `Some(a)` because `a` directly precedes the comment.
312	    ///
313	    /// ## Preceding token and node
314	    ///
315	    /// ```ignore
316	    /// [a, /* comment */]
317	    /// ```
318	    ///
319	    ///  Returns `Some(a)` because `a` is the preceding node of `comment`. The presence of the `,` token
320	    /// doesn't change that.
321	    pub fn preceding_node(&self) -> Option<&SyntaxNode<L>> {
322	        self.preceding.as_ref()
323	    }

328	    }

331	    ///

333	    ///

335	    /// all children children of the [`enclosing_node`](DecoratedComment::enclosing_node) following this comment are tokens.
336	    ///
337	    /// The following node is guaranteed to be a sibling of [`preceding_node`](DecoratedComment::preceding_node).
338	    ///
339	    /// # Examples
340	    ///

342	    ///
343	    /// ```ignore

345	    /// ```
346	    ///

348	    ///

350	    ///

353	    /// ```
354	    ///

356	    ///

Instead, here's a summary of the declaration/colon/value comment handlers described in the content:

## Handlers related to declaration/colon/value comments

**`handle_declaration_name_comment`** — Handles comments after a declaration name. When the preceding node is a declaration name (`AnyCssDeclarationName`):
- If the parent is a `CssGenericProperty`, the comment becomes *dangling* on that property. The doc comment explains this keeps SCSS output like `"a { color // comment\n : red; }"` positioned between the name and colon.
- If the parent is a `CssGenericComponentValueList`, it returns the default placement.
- Otherwise, it attaches the comment as *leading* on the preceding node.

**`handle_generic_property_comment`** — Locates a `CssGenericProperty` ancestor and its name. Key behaviors:
- If the comment falls between the colon and value (via `is_between_property_colon_and_value`), it becomes *trailing* on the property.
- If the comment matches a trailing-trivia piece of the name token, it becomes *dangling*. The inline note describes keeping `"a { color/* comment */: red; }"` between name and colon.
- If the comment sits between the name and a following `CssGenericComponentValueList`, it becomes *trailing*.

**`is_between_property_colon_and_value`** — A helper returning whether a comment start offset lies at or after the colon's trimmed end and before the value's first token start. The comment notes that `"a { color: /* comment */ red; }"` belongs to the colon/value boundary.

**Related SCSS variable handlers:**
- `handle_scss_variable_declaration_comment` — Similar logic for `ScssVariableDeclaration`, handling comments between name/colon and colon/value.
- `is_between_variable_colon_and_value` — The variable-declaration analog of the colon/value boundary check.

These handlers are all chained together in the `place_comment` method of `CssCommentStyle` via `.or_else(...)` calls, with the declaration/colon handlers appearing near the end of that chain.

# @biomejs/biome

## 2.4.10

### Patch Changes

- [#8838](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/8838) [`f3a6a6b`](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/commit/f3a6a6ba446aaac59119453e5becd657e509e22f) Thanks [@baeseokjae](https://github.com/baeseokjae)! - Added new lint nursery rule [`noImpliedEval`](https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/no-implied-eval/).

  The rule detects implied `eval()` usage through functions like `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, and `setImmediate` when called with string arguments.

  ```js
  // Invalid
  setTimeout("alert('Hello');", 100);

  // Valid
  setTimeout(() => alert("Hello"), 100);
  ```

- [#9320](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/9320) [`93c3b6c`](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/commit/93c3b6ca52d4966db2c5b9c37d73c049ffccd1a5) Thanks [@taberoajorge](https://github.com/taberoajorge)! - Fixed [#7664](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/7664): [`noUnusedVariables`](https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/no-unused-variables/) no longer reports false positives for TypeScript namespace declarations that participate in declaration merging with an exported or used value declaration (`const`, `function`, or `class`) of the same name. The reverse direction is also handled: a value declaration merged with an exported namespace is no longer flagged.

**`crates/biome_css_formatter/src/comments.rs`**
- Added `handle_generic_property_comment`, which places a comment found in the property name's trailing trivia (i.e. between the name and the colon) as a **trailing comment of the name** node, keeping it in `color /* comment */:` position instead of moving it before the name.
- Wired the new handler into the `place_comment` chain (before `handle_declaration_name_comment`).

**`crates/biome_css_formatter/src/css/properties/generic_property.rs`**
- Rewrote `fmt_fields` so that comments between the colon and value (attached as trailing comments of the property) are printed inline right after the colon, and then the value is pushed to the next line with one extra indentation level via `indent(hard_line_break + value)`. When there are no such comments, the value stays on the same line.
- Overrode `fmt_trailing_comments` to no-op, since those comments are now emitted manually in `fmt_fields`.

**`crates/biome_css_formatter/src/utils/component_value_list.rs`**
- Added a `OneGroupPerLineWithDanglingComments` layout so multi-group value lists (e.g. `font-family`) still lay out correctly when a colon→value comment is present, keeping the comment inline while breaking the groups.
